title: Catch Difficulty Index: How to Evaluate Chennai Super Kings Beyond Raw Drop Counts
dek: Dropped-catch counts are a blunt way to judge fielders: they ignore how hard each chance was. What would a catch-difficulty index for Chennai Super Kings need, and what can be measured now?
excerpt: Catches account for {{ev:ct-l}} of the rest of the IPL's bowler wickets and {{ev:ct-t}} of Chennai Super Kings'. Without data on drops and difficulty, a fair fielding grade remains out of reach.
author: CricField Editorial Desk
keyTakeaways: {{ev:ct-t}} of Chennai Super Kings' bowler wickets have been catches, against {{ev:ct-l}} for the rest of the IPL.
CSK have {{ev:ct-n}} catches on record in the CricField warehouse.
Drops and catch difficulty are not recorded in public ball-by-ball data.

sections.heading: The Problem With Drop Counts
body: A dropped skier at long-on and a missed half-chance at slip both count as one drop. A fielder who stands in the hardest positions will drop more chances and still be the most valuable catcher in the side.
A catch-difficulty index would weight each chance by how hard it was: reaction time, distance covered, ball speed. Public data does not provide those inputs.

sections.heading: What the Scorebook Does Show
body: {{ev:ct-t}} of Chennai Super Kings' bowler-credited wickets have been catches, against {{ev:ct-l}} for the rest of the league, from {{ev:ct-n}} catches on record.
On this measure their highest season was 2015, at {{ev:ct-x-best-v}}, and their lowest 2010, at {{ev:ct-x-worst-v}}.

sections.heading: Building an Index In-House
body: The inputs for a fair index are achievable with video: the fielder's starting position, distance to the ball and time available. Each chance can then be graded and every fielder rated on catches taken above expectation.
For CSK, that would turn fielding selection from reputation into evidence, and highlight which positions need specialists.

sections.heading: Catch Share Is Not Catching Quality
body: A high share of caught wickets can reflect bowlers inducing false shots rather than fielders taking hard chances. It says nothing about the chances that went down.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Grade the Chance, Not the Fielder's Tally
body: Raw catch and drop counts should not drive Chennai Super Kings' fielding decisions. A graded-chance index, built from video, is the only fair measure.
Until it exists, the honest position is that catching quality cannot be compared between franchises from public data.

methodology: Regulation innings only (super overs excluded). Economy uses runs charged to the bowler (byes and leg-byes excluded) per legal ball times six. Bowler wickets exclude run outs. Generated from the CricField warehouse by scripts/editorial/engine. Catches include caught and caught-and-bowled. Dropped catches are not recorded in Cricsheet data.
